fields.title: Brain cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Brain cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Brain cancer covers various types of brain tumour, including primary tumours that begin in the brain and metastatic tumours that spread from other parts of the body. Israel is known for its innovative approaches to treating this complex disease, which improve both the outlook and patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of brain cancer:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    The standard imaging method for establishing the size, shape and position of a tumour in the brain and how it relates to the structures around it.
  2. Computed tomography (CT):
    Used for a rapid assessment of the brain, particularly after injury or when MRI is not available.
  3. Positron emission tomography (PET):
    Helps check for and assess the spread of the disease.
  4. Biopsy:
    Carried out to obtain an accurate diagnosis of the type of brain cancer, its stage and how aggressive it is likely to be.

Treatments for brain cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Craniotomy: An open operation to remove the tumour, in which the surgeons aim to remove as little healthy tissue as possible.
    • Stereotactic biopsy: A minimally invasive method of taking a sample of the tumour using computer guidance.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • External beam radiotherapy: Uses high-energy beams to destroy the cancer cells.
    • Stereotactic radiosurgery: A technique that allows precise targeting of a tumour in the brain without the need for open surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells and prevent them growing and spreading.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at particular abnormalities in the cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: Stimulates the body's own immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including neurosurgeons, oncologists, radiologists and others ensures a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical technology and treatment techniques.
  • An individual approach: Treatment plans are adapted to the particular patient, taking account of the stage of the disease, general health and other important factors.

Treatment of brain cancer in Israel aims for maximum effectiveness, the preservation of function and quality of life, and the minimisation of side effects and the risk of recurrence.

fields.title: Adrenal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Adrenal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Adrenal cancer is a rare cancer affecting the adrenal glands — small glands situated above the kidneys. In Israel, patients are offered a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, combining innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment in order to achieve the best results.

Diagnosis of adrenal cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    allow a detailed assessment of the adrenal glands and detection of a tumour.
  2. Biochemical tests of blood and urine
    identify the excess hormone production characteristic of some types of adrenal cancer.
  3. Biopsy
    followed by histological analysis of the tissue sample helps establish the type of tumour precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. PET-CT
    is used to identify metastases and assess how far the disease has spread.

Treatments for adrenal cancer

  1. Surgery
    remains the main treatment, involving removal of the tumour together with the adrenal gland.
  2. Radiotherapy
    may be used to reduce symptoms or control metastases.
  3. Chemotherapy
    is used to treat metastatic adrenal cancer, particularly in aggressive forms of the disease.
  4. Biological treatment
    includes medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  5. Radiosurgery in Israel: the CyberKnife
    is an advanced technology that destroys tumour cells precisely and effectively with minimal effect on the surrounding healthy tissue.
  6. The newest developments
    in the treatment of adrenal cancer are innovative methods and medicines at the clinical trial stage, which gives patients access to the most modern therapies.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of adrenal cancer

  • A multidisciplinary approach ensures all-round assessment and treatment, including consultations with oncologists, surgeons, endocrinologists and other specialists.
  • Advanced technology and treatments, including the CyberKnife and biological therapy, make treatment highly effective.
  • Individualised treatment programmes are developed with the particular features of the disease and each patient's needs in mind.
  • Access to the newest developments and participation in clinical trials open up innovative treatments to patients.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatment options for adrenal cancer, from traditional methods through to the latest innovations in oncology, which makes it possible to achieve the best possible results even in the most difficult cases.

fields.title: Liver cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Liver cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Liver cancer is a serious cancer that may arise as a primary disease of the liver or as the spread of another cancer. Israeli clinics offer innovative approaches to treating liver cancer. The combination of highly qualified specialists and the latest medical technology helps achieve the best results.

Diagnosis of liver cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    of the liver allows tumours or abnormalities in the structure of the liver to be detected.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    provide detailed images of the liver, helping establish the size and position of the tumour and whether there are metastases.
  3. Liver biopsy
    a procedure in which a sample of liver tissue is taken for histological examination. It allows the type of cancer to be diagnosed precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Laboratory tests, including blood tests for tumour markers (AFP) and liver function tests, help assess how the liver is working and whether cancer cells are present.
  5. PET-CT is used for a more precise assessment of the stage of the cancer and to identify metastases in other organs.

Treatments for liver cancer

  1. Surgery,
    including liver resection, is the preferred treatment for localised forms of liver cancer.
  2. Liver transplant
    is considered as an option for patients with severe liver damage or where other treatments are ineffective.
  3. Local ablative treatment,
    including radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and microwave ablation. Used to destroy cancer cells in the liver.
  4. Transarterial chemoembolisation (TACE) and radioembolisation
    are treatments in which medicines or radioactive particles are delivered directly to the tumour through the blood vessels.
  5. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new approaches to treating liver cancer, directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at activating the body's immune system.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of liver cancer

  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists
    ensure accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient
    makes it possible to design treatment that best matches their needs and state of health.
  • Innovative treatments,
    including the latest advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy, give patients access to the most modern and effective methods.
  • Comprehensive support for patients at every stage of treatment, from diagnosis through to rehabilitation and follow-up.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach to the treatment of liver cancer, aiming to extend life as far as possible and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Oesophageal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the oesophagus is a malignant growth developing in the tissue of the oesophagus. Effective treatment of this disease requires accurate diagnosis and the use of modern therapies. Israel is known for its advanced medical technology and its highly qualified specialists in oncology.

Diagnosis of oesophageal cancer

  1. Laboratory tests
    Laboratory tests include blood tests for tumour markers and other specific indicators.
  2. Endoscopy
    Endoscopy is the main method of diagnosing oesophageal cancer, allowing the inner surface of the oesophagus to be examined and a biopsy taken from any suspicious areas of tissue.
  3. PET-CT
    Positron emission tomography (PET) combined with computed tomography (CT) helps identify metastases and assess how far the disease has spread. This method allows the position of the tumour to be established precisely and secondary sites of cancer to be identified.
  4. Biopsy
    A biopsy involves taking a sample of tissue from the tumour for examination under the microscope. It is the key method confirming a diagnosis of cancer and establishing the type of tumour, which is important in choosing the right treatment.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for oesophageal cancer

  1. Surgery
    An operation to remove the tumour is the main treatment for oesophageal cancer. Israel makes wide use of minimally invasive techniques such as laparoscopic and robotic surgery, which minimise damage to tissue and speed up recovery.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Chemotherapy is used to destroy cancer cells and prevent them growing. Israel uses modern medicines and combinations that make treatment more effective and reduce side effects.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Radiotherapy is used to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards. Modern methods of irradiation allow precise targeting of the tumour, minimising the effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Targeted therapy is directed at specific molecules involved in the growth and division of cancer cells. Immunotherapy stimulates the patient's immune system to fight the cancer. These methods are highly effective, particularly in treating aggressive forms of oesophageal cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have many years of experience and international recognition in the field of oncology.
  2. Modern technology: The use of the newest diagnostic and treatment methods makes therapy accurate and effective.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of the features of their illness and their general health.
  4. International recognition: Israeli medical centres are known for their successes in treating cancer and attract patients from all over the world.

Treatment of oesophageal cancer in Israel is an opportunity to receive advanced medical care and improve the chances of a successful recovery, thanks to modern methods and high standards of medical practice.
